what_was_compared: The two retained sealed SH99 exports, which artifacts/storage-baseline/dev-corpus.json (v1) froze as its coordination_report and release members. First, that the pre-#740 reading (PyMuPDF, get_text(sort=True)) still reproduces the v1 digests on those bytes, proving the bytes are the same. Second, the v1 frozen text against the v3 frozen text page by page: v3 is whitespace-normalized content-order text through pypdf. Third, the v3 definition read by both engines: PyMuPDF's plain get_text() whitespace-normalized against pypdf's extract_text() whitespace-normalized, page by page, which is the reading v3 freezes.
explained_differences: v1 froze MuPDF's block-sorted text (get_text(sort=True): blocks ordered by their bottom edge, then left edge). No pure-Python or PDFium reading reproduces MuPDF's blocks, so on the same bytes the v1 text differs from the v3 text on every page, even whitespace-normalized (the count is v1_text_whitespace_normalized_equals_v3_text_pages). This is a change of definition, recorded by the schema version, not a reading of the v3 definition that differs between readers.
Under v3 the two readers freeze byte-identical text on all 154 pages, so the v3 digests are reader-independent across PyMuPDF and pypdf on these exports.
The v1 numeric members (known_duplication_bytes, families, target) are untouched by the reader and remain comparable; only the PDF representative-output digests are not.
